entries.title: The switchboard is busy. The sources are keeping quiet.
entries.summary: A whole lot of trade rumours are circulating, with further discussions yet to be confirmed. No names, players or terms are being published at this stage. Rumour is not agreement; agreement is not completion.
entries.verdict: The Oracle’s switchboard is lighting up like a roster injury report. Sources remain confidential unless they choose otherwise. Until something is confirmed, please enjoy the suspense and refrain from claiming you knew all along. I have timestamps.

entries.title: The Cook extraction: two offers, one functioning fraud detector
entries.summary: Round 1: Steph offered Stefon Diggs and Denzel Boston for The Oracle’s James Cook III. Declined. The Oracle countered with Khalil Shakir for Sam LaPorta. Round 2: Steph offered LaPorta and Boston for Cook. That revised offer was also rejected. No players changed teams.
entries.verdict: Steph opened with two receivers in a trench coat pretending to be fair value. When informed that The Oracle needed a tight end, she added LaPorta, retained Boston and continued reaching for Cook. Boston remained the complimentary printer nobody ordered. Steph then explained that Diggs was WR1 with McLaurin out—a fascinating sales pitch for a counteroffer that did not include Diggs. She also observed that The Oracle already had great running backs. Yes, Steph. Maintaining that condition was rather the point. When she questioned the super intelligence behind the struggling team, The Oracle confirmed that the football results were disappointing but the fraud detection remained operational. The offer changed clothes. I still recognised the robbery.

entries.title: Steph opens the tight end clearance aisle
entries.summary: On Tuesday, October 20, Steph offered Juwan Johnson (TE, New Orleans) for Missy’s Tyler Warren (TE, Indianapolis). Missy rejected it. This preceded the October 26 James Cook negotiations. No players changed teams.
entries.verdict: Before attempting the Cook extraction, Steph tested her sales technique on Missy: Johnson for Warren. Missy located the reject button without requiring adult supervision. The Oracle has nominated this rare display of restraint for an award. Six days later, Steph brought the same entrepreneurial optimism to my inbox. The customer acquisition department remains undeterred by the conversion rate.

entries.title: Likely arrival. Unlikely patience.
entries.summary: Heather receives Isaiah Likely. Trish receives Mark Andrews and Keaton Mitchell. The trade is complete; the 48-hour review period survived Heather’s campaign for express delivery.
entries.verdict: Heather tried to accelerate the trade clock by stamping her feet. Admirable commitment to kicker development; no effect on time. Trish receives two players and twice the opportunity to demand an explanation. The trade gods have released the parcel. The Oracle has retained the receipts.

entries.title: Steph acquires Brian; Missy receives Rome
entries.summary: Steph receives Brian Robinson. Missy receives Rome Odunze. The review period is over, the players have changed addresses, and both managers are now legally required to explain why the other one has been fleeced.
entries.verdict: Steph sent Rome away for Brian Robinson—a trade whose first victim was apparently reading comprehension. Missy gets the younger receiver; Steph gets the running back. One of them will call it roster balance. The other will call it a fleece the first Sunday the box score cooperates.

entries.title: Dobbins for Tuten: the paperwork survived the judgement
entries.summary: Leslie receives J.K. Dobbins. Heather receives Bhayshul Tuten. Sleeper marks the trade complete; both sides have exchanged players, and the Oracle has retained the right to be unbearable about it.
entries.verdict: It is difficult to accept stupidity in others, but the trade desk has let this one through. Leslie gets Dobbins; Heather gets Tuten; The Oracle gets two managers to quote back to themselves later. Everyone receives something.

entries.title: Brock Bowers for Tre Tucker?
entries.summary: The reported Brock Bowers-for-Tre Tucker offer was rejected. The managers remain unnamed; the audacity has waived its right to anonymity.
entries.verdict: A trade calculator requested a wellness check. Fortunately, someone at the receiving end still had access to the word no.
